title: The glass
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. Glass. The owner cuts it with a wheel and a snap and a sound the strip draws as a short straight line. Wood tries. Three panes into the bin. The fourth snaps clean. She says the sound was right on the third. He didn't hear it.

panels.composition: The backroom. The OWNER scoring a pane of glass with a wheel cutter on a felt table. A short straight line drawn for the sound. WOOD watching.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses scoring a pane of glass with a wheel cutter on a felt-topped table while a young man watches, a short straight line drawn for the sound, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD's hands on the cutter. The score wandering. The snap: a jagged line. The pane in two wrong pieces.

image.prompt: close on a young man's hands snapping a pane of glass into two uneven pieces along a wandering score, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Three pieces in the glass bin. The fourth pane on the felt. The score straight. The snap: a short straight line.

image.prompt: close on a pane of glass snapped cleanly in two on a felt table beside a bin of broken pieces, black and white, no words
a young man holding up a cleanly cut pane of glass toward a doorway, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The sound is drawn as a line. The third sounded right and broke.
